correctness.rationale: The Heawood graph is the incidence graph of the seven nonzero F_2^3 vectors and their seven orthogonal lines. Every outside point has a trace only in selected lines and vice versa; nonempty injectivity forces p+q>=6 and p in {2,3,4} at size six. Independently traversing all 3003 six-subsets, and all smaller subsets, gives exactly 448 valid six-codes. Fano collinearity types yield 28+84+168+84+84 and direct enumeration of 168 collineations plus duality partitions codes into 28,84,168,168 orbits; this is exhaustive for 14 vertices.

value.rationale: The Heawood incidence graph is the canonical smallest 3-regular girth-six graph, a published location-domination benchmark. The exact optimizer census and four symmetry types distinguish every minimum detector configuration and are an independently useful natural finite classification beyond the known minimum number.

scientific_limitations: Ordinary location domination on one 14-vertex Heawood graph, not identifying codes or all larger codes.
